sections.html:
Aiken, about 20 miles northeast of Augusta, Georgia, is the biggest city in Aiken County and its seat. It had 32,025 residents in 2020, and 33,808 are estimated for 2025. With a median age of 47.6, inherited houses and downsizing moves are routine here, and both can put a house on a tight timeline.

Jobs in the area lean heavily on the Savannah River Site, and a shift at an employer that large can force a household to sell quickly. Older homes near Hopelands Gardens and Hitchcock Woods may also fall under the exterior review rules covered below.

Hot, humid summers and about 51 inches of rain a year are hard on older houses, and roofs, crawl spaces and cooling systems draw the most attention. Inspectors check HVAC age and moisture, and a long repair list can drag out a conventional sale.

If the repairs are more than you want to take on, selling as is ends that negotiation, and state law allows it.

If your address falls in a review area, Aiken's Design Review Board reviews Certificate of Appropriateness applications. The city sets two filing deadlines before a board meeting.

Project typeApplication dueExamples
Complex30 days before the meetingNew construction, demolition, additions, relocations, porch enclosures, work touching more than one exterior historic feature
Simpler14 days before the meetingNon-in-kind window, door or siding replacement, fences, gutters, handicap ramps, painting, paving, screening a porch

Renovating before you list means the review calendar can add weeks. If you sell as is, the buyer inherits the question, and you don't wait on it.

sections.h2: What South Carolina requires of a seller
sections.html:
Selling a home of one to four units usually means handing the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement. The form asks about water and sewer, structure, mechanical systems, wood-destroying insects, zoning, hazards like lead paint and radon, leases and homeowners association rules.

Several kinds of transfer fall outside it:

  • Court-ordered transfers and foreclosure-related transfers.
  • Transfers by a fiduciary, such as an estate representative.
  • Transfers to a spouse or lineal relative.
  • Sales where both sides agree in writing not to complete the form.

South Carolina lets you sell as is, with the buyer still responsible for inspecting. Knowingly false or incomplete answers can leave a seller liable for actual damages and court costs.

Because the State Bar calls every stage of a real estate deal the practice of law, a South Carolina attorney runs the closing, prepares the deed, does the title work and files the deed with the county.

The county Register of Deeds takes Aiken deeds. Find it in the Government Center, 1930 University Parkway, Suite 2100, or call 803-642-2072.

Records there reach back to 1872. Anything recorded after June 12, 2005 is imaged and viewable on office computers, while older documents sit in books. The state fee is $1.85 per $500 of price, with $0.55 of each $1.85 kept by the county. Your closing attorney or the office can give the full total for your deed.

One tax bill a year comes from Aiken County. It can be paid from September 30 through January 15, after which penalties climb: 3 percent starting January 16, then 7 percent more after the second of February and 5 percent more after March 17.

If the owner applied for the legal residence rating, the home is assessed at 4 percent of value, and other residential property at 6 percent. Selling triggers reappraisal, which means the buyer's bill may not match yours.

The state homestead exemption, covering the first $50,000 of value, may already apply if you are 65 or older, disabled or legally blind. Our Aiken County property tax guide lists the assessor and treasurer details.

sections.h2: Planning a fast sale in Aiken
sections.html:
Collect four items before you list or request a cash offer: the deed or estate papers, the newest tax bill, notes on needed repairs, and a list of any exterior work done in a review area. With these in hand the first week goes faster.

Next, decide how much time you have. A listing suits a house in good order. Deferred repairs, several heirs or a tight move date often point to a cash sale, where the buyer needs no mortgage approval and takes the house as it stands. Either way the closing attorney handles title, taxes and recording.

Ask every buyer how fast they can close, whether they want an inspection period and who covers the recording fee, and get the answers in writing.

sections.h2: Estates, downsizing and the disclosure exceptions
sections.html:
Plenty of Aiken sales start with a death or a move to something smaller. An estate representative sells as a fiduciary, and that kind of transfer is excepted from the disclosure statement. Other duties remain, so check with the closing attorney before assuming the form can be skipped.

Gifts and sales to a spouse or lineal relative are excepted as well. Both sides may agree in writing to skip the form, though a buyer who does still carries the inspection risk. Selling as is makes plain who carries what.

Either way, gather paperwork early. Heirs need the death certificate, proof of authority to sell and the deed history, because the attorney's title work starts there.

sections.h2: What the closing day looks like
sections.html:
On closing day the attorney finalizes the deed, reviews the title and sets out the money. Year's taxes are prorated, payoffs go to any lender or lienholder, and the deed is filed with the Register of Deeds, where an image of it can be viewed later.

Bring photo ID and, if someone signs for you, the document that gives that person authority. Ask in advance for a settlement statement so you can see every line before the day. If you have a home still in a review area, tell the attorney about any open Certificate of Appropriateness so the buyer can pick it up.

sections.h2: Check your address before you promise repairs
sections.html:
Before you fix a porch, swap windows or paint, find out whether the house sits in a review area. Painting, fences, gutters and handicap ramps all need a Certificate of Appropriateness there, and the 14-day or 30-day filing window applies before the board meets. A repair done without approval can become the buyer's headache and a delay for you.

Calling the city with your address takes minutes and tells you which path you are on. If the answer is that review applies and your timeline is short, selling as is lets the next owner decide what to change.

sections.h2: A short checklist for Aiken sellers
sections.html:
• Confirm whether the disclosure statement applies to your sale or whether an exception covers you.
  • Check the review area question for exterior work.
  • Get the latest tax bill and note whether the legal residence rating is on file.
  • Ask whether a homestead exemption is in place.
  • Choose a closing attorney early and share your deed and any estate papers.

None of these steps is hard on its own. Trouble comes from finding them out in the last week, when a closing date is set and a buyer is waiting.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems when I sell my Aiken house?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. A written statement is required for most one to four unit sales, except fiduciary and foreclosure transfers, and a false answer can still create liability in an as-is sale.

faqs.q: Does Aiken have historic district review for exterior changes?
faqs.a: Yes, in review areas. The Design Review Board reviews Certificate of Appropriateness applications, due 30 days before a meeting for complex projects and 14 days for simpler ones.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Aiken?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds, 1930 University Parkway, Suite 2100, 803-642-2072. Your attorney usually files it for you.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Aiken house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, as is. State law lets you skip repairs, though disclosure rules and open code or tax liens still apply.
